conventions.editing: This file is canonical JSON. After initial creation, mutate it with jq (or equivalent structure-preserving tooling), not a text editor. Canonical form: `jq -S .` with 2-space indent; re-running that command must be a no-op.
conventions.ids: Items are T-NNN, zero-padded, append-only. Never renumber, never reuse. Dropped items keep their ID with status=dropped and a note.
conventions.ordering: phase (A/B/C/D) is the coarse logical order; order is the sequence within a phase. Both are proposals to be re-sorted by the repo owner, not commitments.
conventions.purpose: Cross-session idea ledger. Captures decisions and suggestions from design discussions so they survive context loss. An item here is preserved, not necessarily approved.

description: Todo ledger for k8s-platform-scenarios, seeded from the 2026-07-06 design discussion on scenario storage, deterministic enforcement, docs-blind authoring, and the first experiment.

items.summary: Create this TODO.json ledger capturing all suggestions from the founding design discussion, with phases, dependencies, and handoff-quality summaries. Done when merged to main.
items.title: Bootstrap the cross-session todo ledger

items.summary: PreToolUse hook (repo .claude/settings.json + scripts/hooks/) that deterministically DENIES WebFetch/WebSearch/Bash calls targeting the platform source (github.com/lago-morph/k8s-platform, raw.githubusercontent.com/lago-morph/k8s-platform, codeload equivalents, git clone/fetch of that repo) while allowing the published docs site (lago-morph.github.io/k8s-platform). This is the docs-blindness contract as enforcement instead of prose. Must land BEFORE any docs-only authoring subagent runs, so isolation is enforced, not promised. Hooks apply to subagent tool calls in-session. Delivered: scripts/hooks/deny-platform-source wired via .claude/settings.json with matcher WebFetch|WebSearch|Bash|mcp__github.*|mcp__Claude_Code_Remote.* — scans tool input for references to the platform source repository (owner/repo path deliberately not written out here, because the hook also scans Bash command text and this summary is passed through one), covering https/ssh/raw/codeload/api URL forms and github-MCP owner+repo params case-insensitively, scrubbing this repository's own -scenarios references first, failing CLOSED on unparseable input. Agent-launch tools deliberately unmatched: probe prompts legitimately contain the forbidden URL as a prohibition, and a subagent's own tool calls are hooked individually. Table-driven tests: scripts/hooks/test-deny-platform-source (19 cases). Verified live: the hook took effect in-session the moment settings.json existed and denied its own author's very next Bash call, whose prose arguments contained the forbidden pattern — enforcement is real and conservative. Network-policy layer remains T-027.
items.title: Docs-blindness boundary hook

items.summary: Create experiments/ directory convention: experiments/NNN-name/ holding loose JSON records from throwaway probes. Deliberately NO schema and NO linting at this stage (records are expected to be discarded); JSON-from-day-one so later hardening has a substrate. Include a small README stating the throwaway expectation. Delivered: experiments/README.md stating the NNN-name convention, the throwaway expectation, and the per-experiment README requirement; scripts/lint-json exempts experiments/ trees to well-formedness-only (no canonical form, no schemas, no semantic checks) per the no-linting decision.
items.title: experiments/ storage for throwaway probe records

items.summary: Launch ONE fresh subagent whose only inputs are: the role, the single scenario bullet, the docs site root URL, and a loose output shape. It attempts a full L1 scenario write (actor, preconditions, prose steps with citations, observable outcome, defect classes) and must record every fact it needed but could not find in the docs, every assumption it was forced to make, and where it blocked. Scenario: S4 (tenant-dev deploys a stateless web application from a git repo via GitOps) - confirmed by the owner 2026-07-06; it is the best-documented path (the sole tutorial plus a how-to), so gaps found there bound everything else. Owner's prediction to test: 5-10 immediate documentation findings from this single write. Deliberately one scenario only: what we learn feeds the docs-side pull process and will change how we do the rest. Sequencing per owner: the jq/canonical-JSON mechanics (T-006, T-007) are reviewed before this probe runs. Delivered 2026-07-06: probe ran docs-blind behind the T-002 hook (self-test 19/19 at launch); output saved verbatim in experiments/001-s4-depth-probe/probe-output.json (agent final message arrived one byte short of well-formed; the single terminating brace was restored, disclosed in the experiment README). Result: 15 candidate documentation findings (12 missing facts + 1 blocked + 2 platform-fact assumptions) vs the predicted 5-10, on the best-documented path. Sole hard block: tenant verification access (no shipped human kubectl path; access guide is contract-stability). Triage deliberately not started - that is T-005 with the owner.
items.title: Depth probe: docs-only L1 write of ONE scenario

items.summary: Read the probe output with the owner; extract candidate documentation findings into loose JSON records (in experiments/, since findings/ schema does not exist yet). Compare count against the 5-10 prediction. These records seed the findings schema design (T-008) with real shapes instead of speculation.
items.title: Triage depth-probe output into draft findings

items.summary: Write a Claude Code skill defining how agents access and modify schema'd, linted documents in this repo: mutate JSON only via jq or equivalent (never text-edit), run the local lint steps explicitly before committing (do not wait for CI to find errors), sort sub-elements alphabetically where order is not semantic, store all JSON pretty-printed in the canonical form so diffs are logical and useful. The skill makes the conventions executable knowledge for every future session. Delivered as .claude/skills/canonical-json-editing/SKILL.md with mutation recipes; structural enforcement by hook/CI remains T-013/T-014.
items.title: Skill: editing schema'd + linted documents

items.summary: Define the canonical JSON form (jq -S: sorted keys, 2-space indent, trailing newline) and the deterministic tooling around it: scripts/lint-json (well-formedness, canonical round-trip, JSON Schema validation per schemas/map.json, per-document semantic checks such as referential integrity and array ordering), scripts/jq-edit (the sanctioned mutation path: jq filter, atomic canonical rewrite, lint), and scripts/validate-schema.py (JSON Schema draft 2020-12; requires python3 jsonschema and fails loudly with exit 2 if missing). schemas/todo.schema.json governs TODO.json as the first schema'd document.
items.title: Canonical JSON formatting rule + linter

items.summary: JSON Schema for findings plus findings/ directory layout. Fields per the charter: scenario id, what was attempted, what the docs said, what happened, which artifact the defect lives in (documentation/implementation/requirements/scenario/undetermined), evidence, run id; plus lifecycle status. First schema to build because findings exist before mature scenarios do. Schema enforcement is what makes the platform-side pull (T-025) mechanical. Tooling ready: the add-governed-doctype skill (.claude/skills/add-governed-doctype/, SKILL-SPEC-e82da89a38) now encodes the full schema+map+linter+proof loop this item follows; storage direction fixed by ADR 0003.
items.title: Findings schema and storage

items.summary: JSON Schema for scenario records at L0 and L1, designed so each level's schema strictly extends the previous level's (L2+ schemas added when needed). Includes the status vocabulary as an enum: draft / ready / blocked-on-docs / blocked-on-platform / deferred / retired, machine-countable from the records. Informed by what the depth probe actually produced, not written speculatively.
items.title: Scenario schema for L0/L1 with status vocabulary

items.summary: Central assumptions registry (assumptions/ as JSON records): statement, type (tool-knowledge / platform-fact / judgment), scope (global | role | surface | explicit scenario list), status (unresolved / resolved-by-citation / converted-to-finding / invalidated), citations. Scenarios reference assumptions by ID instead of restating them, so fundamentally-identical assumptions cannot diverge across scenarios. Known limit, accepted: semantic dedup (same assumption, different words) is not deterministically lintable and stays a review activity - keep the registry small enough to eyeball. The lintable part: shape, referential integrity, and the L1-to-L2 gate (no unresolved platform-fact assumptions in scope).
items.title: Central assumptions registry with scoping

items.summary: Citation object format {url, anchor, exact_quote} where the exact quote is the durable key (numeric section refs break on insertion; heading anchors break on retitle; a verbatim quote is re-findable and checkable). Provide a checker script that fetches each cited URL and verifies the quote still appears - deterministic, CI-able, and quote drift is itself a signal: the documentation changed underneath a scenario, distinguishing docs regression from platform regression.
items.title: Quote-anchored citation format + drift checker

items.summary: pre-commit configuration running the local linters (canonical JSON form, schema validation, referential integrity; citation checker where network-tolerant) so errors surface at commit time, not CI time. Complements, never replaces, the CI backstop.
items.title: pre-commit hooks for local lint feedback

items.summary: GitHub Actions workflow running every linter on every PR. This is the unskippable deterministic backstop that does not depend on any agent's obedience or any human's vigilance; local hooks and Claude Code hooks are conveniences layered above it.
items.title: CI lint gate on every PR

items.summary: PreToolUse hook denying the Edit/Write tools on canonical JSON paths (scenarios/, findings/, assumptions/), forcing mutations through Bash+jq per the editing skill. Deliberately deferred until schemas are stable enough that the friction pays for itself; before that it just slows the experiments.
items.title: jq-only mutation enforcement hook

items.summary: Adopt the adr skill's output at docs/adr/ with one addition: every ADR carries an enforcement field naming the lint rule / hook / CI check that operationalizes it, or explicitly 'advisory'. A meta-linter fails CI if an ADR references a check that does not exist. The advisory count is reported as a tracked metric (visible debt), exactly like the blocked-on-docs count. Rationale: an ADR nobody checks is worse than no ADR - it manufactures the illusion of governance.
items.title: ADR practice with named enforcement per decision

items.summary: Convention plus implementation: every linter failure message names the ADR it enforces and one line of why. Violation time is the only moment an ADR reliably gets read, so that is where the reference lives - not in prose nobody revisits.
items.title: Linter errors cite the ADR they enforce

items.summary: SessionStart hook that deterministically injects the ADR index (titles + one-liners) and the top open TODO items into every session's context. Prominence stops depending on an agent choosing to read docs/adr/ or TODO.json.
items.title: SessionStart injection of ADR index + open todos

items.summary: Write CLAUDE.md explicitly as documentation OF the enforcement layer - what the hooks block and why, where the linters live, what the canonical formats are - so a denied tool call or failed lint is explicable. It is never itself the enforcement; the repo owner's experience is that prose rules alone are not worth the electrons.
items.title: CLAUDE.md as documentation of checks, not rules

items.summary: Record the already-settled decisions as ADRs once the enforcement-field practice exists, so each is born either enforced or explicitly advisory: (1) scenario IDs freeze the brainstorm numbering S01-S39, append-only from S40, never renumbered; (2) storage is one directory per scenario under scenarios/ with JSON canonical records; (3) findings live in this repo and are PULLED by the platform repo (no cross-boundary pushes in either direction); (4) canonical data is JSON, human-facing views are generated. Partially landed 2026-07-06: three settled-decision ADRs adopted into docs/adr/ (0001 canonical-JSON/jq-edit = ADR-f68da1c75c; 0002 TODO.json ledger = ADR-67f1b0b991; 0003 findings pulled by consumers = ADR-a1e6164091), docs/adr/ bootstrapped with template + index README via the adr skill, each ADR naming its enforcement in Consequences. Remaining: scenario-ID-freeze and per-scenario storage-layout ADRs, pending scenario work.
items.title: ADRs for settled decisions (IDs, layout, pull model, JSON-canonical)

items.summary: Maturity level becomes computed, not claimed: the linter derives the effective level from record content plus checklist attestation fields (for non-machine-derivable facts like 'cleanup verified re-entrant', recorded with who/when), and a record claiming a level above its computed level fails. Advancement L(n) to L(n+1) is then a diff that makes the linter agree, including the gate: no unresolved platform-fact assumptions in scope at L1-to-L2.
items.title: Computed maturity levels with attestation checklists

items.summary: Script that deterministically reports the blocked-on-docs count (and per-status counts generally) from scenario records. The charter designates this count as THE documentation quality metric; it should be one command, not a judgment.
items.title: blocked-on-docs metric as a one-command report

items.summary: Reclassify scenario S1 (full platform rebuild) to L0 blocked-on-docs in the catalog: the charter's parenthetical 'already at L4 - this is the existing clean-build loop' asserts maturity from implementation knowledge, but no rebuild documentation, owner-facing status story, or remediation guidance exists on the docs site, so by the corpus's own definitions it cannot be past L0. Record the charter's claim itself as a finding once findings/ exists - the founding documents are not exempt from the blindness discipline.
items.title: Demote S1 to L0 blocked-on-docs; file the charter-claim finding

items.summary: Mark author-role scenarios S19 and S20 (blog demo scripts) as deferred in the catalog with the reason recorded: they require a hybrid docs+blog context the owner does not want to design yet. Wave-1 work proceeds with owner, tenant, and adversary roles only.
items.title: Defer author scenarios S19/S20 with recorded reason

items.summary: Breadth sweep across remaining wave-1 scenarios: one fresh docs-only subagent PER scenario (per-scenario agents keep isolation pure - one scenario's docs reading must not color another's assessment), each returning a small JSON record: 3-4 sentence scenario sketch, citations found, facts needed but not found, blocked or not. Aggregating the missing-facts fields is the documentation gap map. Deferred in favor of the single depth probe (T-004); revisit after the probe's findings have fed the docs-side pull process.
items.title: Breadth sweep: per-scenario docs-only gap map

items.summary: Document the stable pull contract the platform repo can rely on to extract findings from this repo and materialize them as issues (and potentially feed its documentation-generation process): file layout, schema version, status semantics, finding ID as the idempotency key. The pull implementation and the issue mapping live entirely on the platform side; finding records here never need back-writes. Open question captured from discussion: how findings integrate into the docs-generation workflow on that side - expect discoveries there to change things here.
items.title: Findings pull contract for the platform repo

items.summary: File a finding/request to the platform repo: documentation headings need explicit stable anchor IDs so citations survive retitles. Cheap on the docs-source side; until then the quote-anchored citation format (T-011) carries durability.
items.title: Request stable heading anchors in platform docs

items.summary: For dedicated scenario-authoring sessions, configure the remote-environment network policy to allowlist only the published docs domain. This is the strongest form of the blindness boundary (the hook layer can be evaded by indirection; a network policy cannot). Environment-level configuration, not repo-level.
items.title: Network-policy allowlist for authoring sessions

items.summary: Generator that renders human-facing views (catalog overview, findings report, gap map, per-status counts) as Markdown from the canonical JSON. Humans read renders; machines own the records. Never hand-edit a rendered view.
items.title: Human-facing report generator from canonical JSON

items.summary: Author the remaining wave-1 scenarios to L1 using docs-only subagents behind the hardened schemas, templates, and assumption registry - only after the depth probe's lessons (and any docs-side changes they trigger) are absorbed.
items.title: Batch wave-1 L1 authoring behind hardened substrate

items.summary: Run the self-retrospective skill at meaningful session ends so process lessons are harvested before context loss; first one after the depth-probe experiment. The retrospective's proposed rules and ADR drafts feed back into this ledger.
items.title: Retrospective habit at session boundaries

items.summary: scripts/validate-schema.py — and therefore scripts/lint-json and scripts/jq-edit, which invoke it — requires the python3 jsonschema package, which is NOT present in fresh remote-session containers. The first JSON mutation of a new session fails with validate-schema exit 2 (schema validation cannot run) until pip install jsonschema is run by hand; the canonical-json-editing skill documents the dependency but nothing installs it, so every fresh session hits this wall before it can touch any canonical document. Make the dependency deterministically present: a SessionStart hook or a repo setup/bootstrap script that installs it (candidate: the session-start-hook skill), and/or a pinned requirements file the environment provisions. Discovered live while executing T-004 in a fresh container. Local/session counterpart to T-013 (CI installs its own deps).
items.title: Ensure jsonschema is installed so the JSON linter runs in fresh sessions
